architectural_model: Rauh (provisional: sympodial shoots whose tips abort each year, a side bud taking over; the crown is built of relayed, zig-zag limbs)

variants.name: young
variants.note: a young tree with a pale, straight stem and a narrow, upright crown

variants.name: mature
variants.note: the file as written: a massive leaning trunk forking low into sinuous pale limbs

variants.note: a giant of the floodplain, often several trunks from one base, leaning far out or lying along the ground and rising again, the limbs white against the sky

description: A huge, often leaning tree 15-30 m tall whose bark flakes off in patches, leaving the trunk and limbs a patchwork of white, cream, pale green and tan, with big, deeply five-lobed, fuzzy leaves and bristly seed balls hanging on long stalks in strings of two to seven. It stands on the gravel benches and banks of the larger creeks and rivers, Weber Creek and the Cosumnes, where water runs under the gravel all summer.

season_notes.winter: Bare white and mottled limbs stand out along the river, hung with brown seed balls that break up into fluff over the winter.
season_notes.spring: New leaves come out woolly and pale in March and April, with small green flower balls on hanging strings.
season_notes.summer: Broad leaves give a patchy, open shade; a fungus often browns the spring leaves, and the tree puts out a second flush.
season_notes.fall: Leaves go dull tan and brown, rarely bright, and drop through November and December.

riparian.water: Roots in the coarse gravel and cobble of floodplains where water flows under the bed through the summer, even when the surface dries.

notes: California (western) sycamore is the big tree of the gravel floodplains of California's larger streams, from the coast and the Central Valley into the Sierra foothills below about 1,000 m: on Weber Creek, the Cosumnes and the American, on the cobble bars and first benches where water flows under the bed all summer (permanence intermittent: its roots find the underflow when the surface dries). Orders [3, 7]: it lines the larger creeks and the rivers, rarely a small creek. A tree 15-30 m (file 15-26, veteran to 32), dbh 0.6-1.5 m (radius_ratio 0.05), the trunk very often leaning or even lying along the ground before rising, and forked low into two or three great sinuous limbs (trunk.length_ratio 0.32, split_prob 0.65, lean_deg 18, veteran 28 with up to three leaders): decurrent, a broad, irregular, open crown. The limbs zig-zag (level zigzag_deg) because the shoots are sympodial. Bark: the signature of the tree. On the trunk and limbs thin plates flake away, leaving a patchwork of white, cream, pale green-grey and tan, almost white on the upper limbs; only the base of old trunks is dark brown and furrowed. bark_pattern 'mottled' is a new pattern name that the client does not draw yet and will learn: bark_rgb is the mean pale grey-cream (200, 192, 176), and bark.mottle proposes what the pattern needs (the patch colours white, pale green-grey and tan, patch size 5-30 cm, and a darker, furrowed band of base_m at the foot of old trunks); until the client reads it, the trunk draws plain in the mean colour. Leaves alternate, 12-25 cm, palmately three- to five-lobed with deep, pointed lobes (deeper than the eastern sycamore's), woolly when young and fuzzy beneath all summer: leaf_shape lobed_large as big-leaf maple's (lobes 5, lobe_depth 0.5, lobe_style palmate), leaf_size_m 0.2; a quarter of the palette lightened for the pale felted undersides. Summer colour a light, slightly yellowish green; anthracnose browns many spring leaves in wet years (not drawn). Fall colour dull tan to brown (fall tint 166, 134, 82; r/g about 1.6), leaves dropping late through November and December. Fruit: bristly balls 2-3 cm in strings of two to seven on a long hanging stalk, staying on the bare tree into winter; not drawn (no hanging-ball fruit form). The trunks are cavity trees for woodpeckers and the crowns nest sites for hawks (cover_for). Snags are few: 4% of the veteran slots, pale. Architectural model provisional.
